Thing from the Stars encounter and appearance rules

heroes.name: Crusader
heroes.summary: A durable frontline fighter who can strike, stun, protect himself, and provide small health and stress recovery.

overview.positions: Ranks 1 and 2 keep Smite and Stunning Blow available. Rank 3 is a situational alternative for Holy Lance, which advances the Crusader when used.
strengths: Durable frontline fighter with strong melee damage.
Can stun front enemies and deal bonus damage to Unholy foes.
Offers small party health, stress, and torch recovery.
weaknesses: Very low base Speed means many enemies and allies may act first.
Most direct attacks are limited to the front; Holy Lance is needed to reach back ranks.
overview.beginnerAdvice: Start in rank 1 or 2 and use Smite or Stunning Blow against a front threat. If the party is shuffled, Holy Lance can reach deeper enemies and move him forward.

gallery.alt: User-provided Darkest Dungeon-style illustration identified as Crusader

editorial.description: A direct frontline strike that deals bonus damage to Unholy enemies.
editorial.whenToUse: Use against a priority enemy in rank 1 or 2, especially if it is Unholy.

editorial.description: A ranged attack that hits both front enemy ranks at the same time.
editorial.whenToUse: Use when both front ranks are worth damaging. This splits damage, so focus fire may be better when removing one enemy would prevent its next action.

editorial.description: A frontline strike that can stun one enemy, making it lose its next turn if the stun succeeds.
editorial.whenToUse: Use to delay a dangerous front enemy. Stun resistance can prevent the effect.

effects.text: The PROT bonus and self-mark last 1 battle.

editorial.description: Hardens the Crusader and marks him, drawing attacks toward him for a short time.
editorial.whenToUse: Use when the Crusader can take the incoming hits and you want to protect a more vulnerable ally.

editorial.description: Restores a small amount of health to one ally in any party position.
editorial.whenToUse: Use to stabilize a wounded ally when the Crusader does not need to attack.

editorial.description: A lunging strike that reaches the enemy back ranks and moves the Crusader forward.
editorial.whenToUse: Use after the Crusader has been pushed back, or when the enemy back line is the priority. Check the party formation after he advances.

combatSkills.name: Inspiring Cry
combatSkills.category: Party support · Heal and stress relief

editorial.description: Gives every party member a small heal and reduces stress, while raising the torchlight.
editorial.whenToUse: Use when the party needs a little recovery or the torchlight needs a boost.

bosses.name: Necromancer
bosses.summary: An Unholy/Eldritch Ruins boss who retreats as he summons skeletons, steadily changing the enemy formation.

mechanics.text: The Necromancer starts in the front rank. Attacking moves him back one rank and normally summons a skeleton; a stun or three existing skeletons prevents that summon.
Skeleton minions summoned by the Necromancer are linked to him and are removed when he is defeated.
At higher difficulties, summoned Bone Soldiers can begin with Stealth; higher tiers can also summon Bone Defenders that Guard him.

attacks.text: The Flesh Is Willing attacks the front ranks while summoning a skeleton.
The Clawing Dead pressures the rear ranks while summoning a skeleton.
Six Feet Under targets the party with stress pressure and summons a skeleton.

tacticalConsiderations.text: Editorial: plan to reach the rear ranks as he retreats; the source guide describes back-rank pressure as a practical way to shorten the fight.
Editorial: his listed Bleed and Blight resistance is lower than his Stun resistance, but this does not account for other Ruins enemies or party constraints.

bosses.name: Swine Prince
bosses.summary: A large Beast boss supported by Wilbur, whose marks set up the Prince’s strongest attacks.

mechanics.text: The Swine Prince occupies enemy ranks 1–3; Wilbur stands in rank 4.
Wilbur marks one or two heroes, and the Prince can answer those marks with focused attacks. With no marks, the Prince uses Wild Flailing instead.
Damaging Wilbur while the Prince is alive triggers Enraged Destruction against the whole party. Defeating Wilbur first makes the Prince use that attack each round.

attacks.text: End This One and End These Two are Wilbur’s mark skills.
Obliterate Body and Obliterate Masses target marked heroes.
Enraged Destruction is the response to damaging Wilbur while the Prince remains alive.
Bit ’o Squeal can stun the party at higher quest levels.

tacticalConsiderations.text: Editorial: concentrate attacks on the Swine Prince and avoid damaging Wilbur while the Prince is still alive; this follows the source guide’s warning about Enraged Destruction.
Editorial: be cautious with Riposte because an automatic counter can hit Wilbur and trigger the same retaliation.

bosses.name: Hag
bosses.summary: A Human boss positioned behind a cauldron that captures a party member and forces the rest to adapt.

mechanics.text: The Hag occupies ranks 3–4; the cauldron occupies ranks 1–2. Neither can be moved.
Into the Pot! captures one hero. The captive cannot act and takes damage as turns pass; damaging the filled pot can release them, after which the pot can be used again.
When the captive reaches Death’s Door, the pot releases them. Defeating the Hag also releases the captive and ends the encounter.
The Hag has multiple actions per round and uses party attacks and stress effects while a hero is trapped.

attacks.text: Into the Pot! selects a hero and places them in the cauldron.
Meat Tenderizer attacks the heroes outside the pot.
Season to Perfection applies a damage and accuracy debuff; Taste the Stew is used in relation to a trapped hero.

tacticalConsiderations.text: Editorial: bring attacks that can reach ranks 3–4 and expect the active party formation to shift when someone is captured.
Editorial: the source recommends balancing damage to the Hag with timely recovery for a hero released at critical health; the cauldron’s occupant cannot use skills while trapped.

bosses.name: Siren
bosses.summary: An Eldritch boss with two actions per round who can charm an equipped hero and turn that hero against the party.

mechanics.text: The Siren takes two turns per round.
Song of Desire can charm one hero. The controlled hero can use equipped combat skills, then returns to the party in rank 4 after the charm ends.
A charmed hero is placed in a rank adjacent to the Siren and takes stress while controlled; the charm can also target heroes in Stealth.
The Siren can summon Pelagic enemies and use attacks that apply party-wide Bleed or stress.

attacks.text: Song of Desire is the hero-control ability.
Pressure Crash targets the party with stress damage.
Devour applies Bleed; High Tide can summon an aquatic reinforcement.

tacticalConsiderations.text: Editorial: prepare for the party to operate with three heroes while one is charmed, and expect the returning hero to re-enter at the back.
Editorial: use area attacks carefully while a controlled party member is among the enemies; keep movement options available to restore formation.
